headlines.title_original: Election exit polls: Majority of voters back opposition, but Netanyahu's Likud emerges as largest party
headlines.summary_original: Exit polls from major television channels show Netanyahu's Likud is projected to win approximately 50 seats, despite rival Eisenkot bloc with more seats – 53. Neither is set to win a 61-seat majority, without the Arab parties, which gained around 17

headlines.title_original: Israel's Elections Committee rejects Likud petition to extend voting hours

headlines.title_original: High voter turnout could push out smaller right-wing parties, hurting Netanyahu's bloc
headlines.summary_original: The overall turnout measured by 8 P.M. across Israel was the highest ever recorded up to that hour, and the electoral threshold could be as high as 210,000 votes – potentially pushing out both hardliner Ofer Winter and the unaligned Reservists

headlines.title_original: Can Republican scandals give Democrats an opening in red Ohio?

headlines.title_original: Inside the propaganda machine: How Netanyahu's campaign messages spread

headlines.title_original: Netanyahu films campaign ad at Israeli city hall in violation of election law

headlines.title_original: We found the few Israelis who aren't voting – and are willing to talk about it
headlines.summary_original: Israelis' disillusionment with politics did not deter them from breaking voter turnout records by noon. But throughout the day, some were still undecided about whom to vote for – if at all. 'I don't believe Bibi or Gadi,' one said. 'I only trust God'
